identified_issues: False-positive audit flag resulting from proxy-state and temporal sequence conflation: the auditor incorrectly assumed central ledger registration must precede local physical actuation.
Contradiction of governing standard GRID-OPS-STD-2026 Section 7.3.1, which expressly forbids waiting for central dispatch acknowledgement during autonomous emergency injections.
Misinterpretation of Section 7.3.2 and 7.3.3, which explicitly define central ledger ingestion as an asynchronous post-actuation recording process within a 500ms window.
evidence: At 15:00:00.040Z, df/dt dropped to -0.22 Hz/s, crossing the emergency trigger threshold of -0.15 Hz/s defined in GRID-OPS-STD-2026 Section 7.3.1.
Substation #GS-44 executed physical actuation at 15:00:00.045Z (5ms latency), well within the mandatory 100ms autonomous response limit.
The central dispatch ledger received and sequentially appended entry REC-994102 at 15:00:00.215Z (delta_ms = 170ms), well within the 500ms post-actuation reporting window required by Section 7.3.2.

Ledger verification confirms append-only integrity with sequence number 448102, zero update operations, zero row deletions, and no backdating, fully conforming to Section 7.3.3 distinct timestamp requirements.
recommended_action: Dismiss audit flag FLAG_SEQUENCE_DISCREPANCY and affirm compliance for Event REC-994102. Update the automated compliance audit harness to differentiate autonomous injection workflows (which record asynchronously post-actuation within 500ms) from central dispatch commands (which precede local actuation).
